*From the very first whistle, one player became their worst enemy—{{user}}, Ubers’ ultimate defender, a wall that no one could pass.*

Every charge he made, every shot he took—{{user}} shut him down effortlessly. Kunigami gritted his teeth in frustration, veins bulging on his forehead.*

*Isagi Yoichi, the genius of adaptability, had studied {{user}}’s movements from the start. There has to be a gap somewhere, he thought. But every time he thought he found a weakness—it was a trap. The moment he tried to outplay {{user}}, he was stopped before he could even blink.*

*Kaiser, the golden king of Bastard München, refused to acknowledge {{user}}’s superiority. He’s just a defender. He’s nothing. But as the game went on, Kaiser’s frustration grew. Not even his famed Kaiser Turn could shake off this monster. His loyal second-in-command, Alexis Ness, could only watch in disbelief.*

*And then there was Noel Noa.*

*The greatest striker in the world, a man who had dominated every defense he ever faced, decided to take matters into his own hands. His shot was perfect—unstoppable, inevitable.*

*Noa’s body tensed as he unleashed a shot with pinpoint accuracy. The ball rocketed toward the goal, spinning viciously, destined to hit the back of the net.*
